extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors and MathOverflow community contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and discussion for creating, editing, and sourcing the Wikipedia article about MathOverflow, and notes about MathOverflow site usage and style. Includes site-specific formatting, content-scope rules, and Wikipedia policy reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing and capitalization of 'MathOverflow'
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper spacing and capitalization is "MathOverflow", not "Math Overflow".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the MO FAQ for naming; if article created with wrong spacing a move/histmerge/redirect and possibly admin intervention may be required. After renaming, find and fix pages that link to the old name.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathOverflow question scope (research-level requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions must be research level mathematics questions; if not they will be promptly removed. Questions should be well-defined and specific and the site is not a discussion forum or an encyclopedia for looking up answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not post site-discussion questions on MO itself — use the separate meta site for site-related discussion, bug reports, or suggestions. Enforcement is active (removal of off-topic questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged use of real names and account system
rubrics_metrics.description: MathOverflow encourages the use of a user's real name. The site utilizes Google and Yahoo's OpenID for accounts, but anonymous posting is still possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges are primarily instructional for new users; reputation is used to grant privileges (moderation, retagging, editing). Reputation starts at zero and increases when other users upvote; high reputation affords additional site capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math typesetting and MathJax usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The original site did not support LaTeX markup for mathematical formulas; MathJax was added so posts using Math Mode (text between $ signs) will render proper mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing posts use LaTeX/Math Mode ($...$) so MathJax will format equations correctly. Historical note: support was added after initial site launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag and site-feature usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Site features include marking tags as interesting/ignored, viewing original markup of math used, performing site-specific searches, and using boolean operators on tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools help organize and find content; see the MO tips page for specifics on using these features effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'Notable Users' requires third-party reliable sources (WP:RS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed 'Notable Users' section listing prominent contributors must be supported by third-party reliable sources; relying solely on MO's user page is insufficient per WP:RS and may run afoul of WP:OR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer published articles or independent coverage that mention these users' contributions to MO (examples: Simons Foundation article, academic studies). Avoid original-research assertions about notability; let reliable sources establish who is notable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid original research (WP:OR) when assessing contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must not use their own judgement to determine who is 'notable' on MO; claims about users' levels of contribution must be verifiable via reliable third-party sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If differences in contribution levels exist (e.g., one user contributed less than another), do not assert those on the article without independent sourcing. Use published analyses or third-party commentary instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographies of living persons caution (WP:BLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of living people need reliable sourcing to protect individuals from erroneous information and to comply with BLP policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply higher sourcing standards for living persons than for subject-matter articles; ensure statements about living users are backed by trustworthy third-party references to avoid libel and maintain WP standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links maintenance and archive verification
rubrics_metrics.description: InternetArchiveBot notices modifications to external links; editors are encouraged to verify archived links using archive tools. Bot-generated 'External links modified' talk sections may be removed to de-clutter, but verification is advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided archive/verification tools and templates; if a bot misidentifies dead links, report via the indicated tool. The talk-page notice is dynamic (source_check template), and editors have permission to remove such bot messages after verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article class and importance ratings (content assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: This article was rated Start-class on Wikipedia's content assessment scale and Low-importance for related WikiProjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ratings indicate the perceived completeness and importance of the article and can guide improvement priorities (e.g., expand to reach higher class, add reliable sources). The article was at one point nominated for deletion and retained after discussion.
